import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1106

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1064](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1106)
-/

open Nat Finset Filter Topology

namespace Erdos1106

/-- The partition function p(n) is the number of ways to write n as a sum of positive
integers (where the order of the summands does not matter). -/
def p : ℕ → ℕ := fun n => Fintype.card (Nat.Partition n)

/--
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$∏_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, then $F(n)$ tends to infinity when $n$ tends to infinity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1106.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun n => #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, p i).primeFactors) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$∏_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, $F(n)>n$ for sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1106.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, p i).primeFactors > n := by
  sorry

end Erdos1106

findings.description: The docstring writes ∏_{i=1}^n p(n), with a constant integrand, instead of ∏_{i=1}^n p(i). The Lean statement correctly uses `p i`. These products have different prime-factor counts: at n = 3 the docstring's product is 27, with one distinct prime factor, whereas the intended product is 6, with two.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1106 defines F(n) as the number of distinct prime factors of ∏_{1≤k≤n} p(k).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `p(n)` inside the docstring's product with `p(i)`. Keep the Lean mathematical statement unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring repeats the constant-integrand typo ∏_{i=1}^n p(n). The source and Lean statement instead use the cumulative product p(1)⋯p(n). This is a documentation error, not a misformalization of the Lean theorem.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1106 asks whether F(n)>n for all sufficiently large n, with F(n) defined using ∏_{1≤k≤n} p(k).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `p(n)` inside the docstring's product with `p(i)`. Keep the Lean mathematical statement unchanged.

status_issues.source_status: The source explicitly records an affirmative solution to F(n)→∞. It attributes an argument to Schinzel using Tijdeman's result and the partition asymptotic, with details in Erdős–Ivić [ErIv90], p. 69. It also records the stronger bound F(n) ≫ log n proved by Schinzel–Wirsing [ScWi87]. The overall page remains OPEN because the stronger question in part (ii) remains open.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1106: “Schinzel noted in the Oberwolfach problem book that F(n)→∞ follows from the asymptotic formula for p(n) and a result of Tijdeman”; subsequently, “Schinzel and Wirsing [ScWi87] have proved F(n) ≫ log n.”
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark part (i) `category research solved`, replace its answer with `answer(True)`, and document the affirmative result and reference. Leave part (ii) open.
